{"assessment":"I read all three files before choosing edits. The prose is technically careful, but it is often written as runs of short declarative sentences that state a constraint and then add a separate qualifier. That makes the argument feel stunted. Below are 24 paragraph replacements: 10 in the analysis chapter, 8 in the evaluation chapter and 6 in the appendix. Each edit joins related claims with connectives that show cause, contrast and consequence. Each also keeps every citation, cross-reference, LaTeX command, path, number and scientific qualification. Clear short sentences are kept where they carry a boundary claim on their own (for example, "No fitted coefficient is available in this first pass" and "Evaluation must preserve these distinctions").

I deliberately left several things unchanged:
- Tables, captions, equations and the enumerated diagnostic cases.
- The quoted model instruction and the JSON example.
- Paragraphs that already read well (the carryover, pilot reuse, behavior-as-outcome, qualitative and release-manifest material).

The edits change no design facts. Questionnaires are still administered only at the end but referenced to each block, the study is still 40 trials per block across two blocks, and practice still uses the first assigned voice. No empirical results are implied, and the text still separates what was inspected from what was validated on a device.","edits":[{"file":"chapters/06-analysis.tex","old":"A prespecified low-complexity function of theta will allow nonlinearity; nominal-angle strata will support balance plots and a categorical sensitivity analysis. Zero-degree trials will remain in the analysis, and completion time will not be divided by angle. The model's random-effects structure, angle function and smallest meaningful effect will be finalized with simulation before confirmatory recruitment. Participant count will be justified under that same model; repeated trials will not be treated as independent participants.","new":"Nonlinearity in starting difficulty will be represented by a prespecified low-complexity function of theta, while nominal-angle strata will support balance plots and a categorical sensitivity analysis. Zero-degree trials will remain in the analysis, and completion time will not be divided by angle. Before confirmatory recruitment, simulation will be used to finalize the model's random-effects structure, angle function and smallest meaningful effect. The participant count will be justified under that same model rather than by treating repeated trials as independent participants.","reason":"Joins fragmented planning statements into connected prose without changing what is prespecified."},{"file":"chapters/06-analysis.tex","old":"Retrospective condition-specific ratings will be collected only after both blocks, with actual survey timestamps retained. Reference scope remains participant-by-block. Recall and recency effects will be considered when interpreting condition differences; these are not immediate post-block measurements. Individual workload dimensions and complete unweighted workload means will be summarized by participant and block. IMI subscales and the three six-item agent-perception constructs will remain separate scores. The additional Guo Q20--22 appealing, eerie and familiar ratings will be analyzed individually, without a combined eeriness score. Voice similarity will be a manipulation check. Custom experience ratings and self-reported guidance use will be analyzed individually. Multiplicity families and secondary contrasts will be specified before confirmatory analysis.","new":"Condition-specific ratings will be collected retrospectively, only after both blocks, with actual survey timestamps retained; each rating set nevertheless remains referenced to a participant-by-block observation. Because these are not immediate post-block measurements, recall and recency effects will be considered when interpreting condition differences. Individual workload dimensions and complete unweighted workload means will be summarized by participant and block. IMI subscales and the three six-item agent-perception constructs will remain separate scores, and the additional Guo Q20--22 appealing, eerie and familiar ratings will be analyzed individually rather than combined into an eeriness score. Voice similarity will serve as a manipulation check, while custom experience ratings and self-reported guidance use will also be analyzed individually. Multiplicity families and secondary contrasts will be specified before confirmatory analysis.","reason":"Consolidates a chain of choppy declaratives; makes the final-only administration with block-referenced scope explicit and logically linked to the recall caveat."},{"file":"chapters/06-analysis.tex","old":"Raw attempts, incorrect selections, pause intervals, timeouts, technical failures and withdrawals will be retained. Stopped trials will not be coded as successful completion times. Timeout/censoring rules and the missing-data estimand will be specified before collection; slow trials will not be removed solely for being slow. Missing responses will not be replaced with zero. Questionnaire scores will follow the complete-subscale rule, with item-level missingness reported. Disliking or failing to recognize a cloned voice will not by itself exclude a participant.","new":"Raw attempts, incorrect selections, pause intervals, timeouts, technical failures and withdrawals will all be retained, and stopped trials will not be coded as successful completion times. Timeout and censoring rules, together with the missing-data estimand, will be specified before collection so that slow trials are not removed solely for being slow. Missing responses will not be replaced with zero; questionnaire scores will instead follow the complete-subscale rule, with item-level missingness reported. Disliking or failing to recognize a cloned voice will not by itself exclude a participant.","reason":"Improves rhythm and shows how the retention, censoring and scoring rules relate to one another."},{"file":"chapters/06-analysis.tex","old":"Engineering analysis will distinguish event qualification, decision latency, model deferral, scheduling delay and actual playback. Because a cue can be judged only in context, sequence-level review will include what happened before and after it. Automatic checks and ratings produced by an offline language-model evaluator (Chapter~\ref{ch:evaluation}) will remain advisory engineering evidence rather than participant perception scores.","reason":"Connects related evaluation commitments and gives a reason for sequence-level review."},{"file":"chapters/06-analysis.tex","old":"The exponentiated voice coefficient, $\exp(\beta_V)$, is a conditional multiplicative time contrast under this model. The conditional coefficient will be reported separately as a model parameter, not substituted for that estimand. Predictions on the original seconds scale require an explicit retransformation procedure and uncertainty estimate. It will vary plausible residual variation, participant intercept variation, voice-slope variation, and missingness. The same model intended for the final analysis will be fitted to each simulated dataset. Convergence, bias, interval coverage, and power or precision will be summarized across candidate enrollment sizes. The chosen smallest meaningful time ratio and assumptions will be documented before recruitment. Synthetic pilot values used to test the workflow will be labeled as such and will not be presented as empirical variance estimates.","new":"The proposed simulation workflow will generate participants with both voice blocks and the intended nominal-angle quotas, varying plausible residual variation, participant intercept variation, voice-slope variation, and missingness. The chosen smallest meaningful time ratio and its supporting assumptions will be documented before recruitment. Synthetic pilot values used to test the workflow will be labeled as such and will not be presented as empirical variance estimates.","reason":"Presents the simulation workflow as a connected procedure rather than a list of separate sentences."},{"file":"chapters/06-analysis.tex","old":"Tracking loss can affect guidance and measurement simultaneously. Each analysis will report its denominator and reasons for missingness.","new":"Tracking loss can affect guidance and measurement simultaneously, though not always in the same way. Predictions on the original seconds scale require an explicit retransformation procedure and uncertainty estimate. No fitted coefficient is available in this first pass.
edits.reason: Makes the conditional-versus-marginal logic explicit; keeps the short closing boundary statement.

edits.old: The proposed simulation workflow will generate participants with both voice blocks and the intended nominal-angle quotas. It will vary plausible residual variation, participant intercept variation, voice-slope variation, and missingness. The same model intended for the final analysis will be fitted to each simulated dataset. Convergence, bias, interval coverage, and power or precision will be summarized across candidate enrollment sizes. The chosen smallest meaningful time ratio and assumptions will be documented before recruitment. Synthetic pilot values used to test the workflow will be labeled as such and will not be presented as empirical variance estimates.
edits.new: The proposed simulation workflow will generate participants with both voice blocks and the intended nominal-angle quotas, varying plausible residual variation, participant intercept variation, voice-slope variation, and missingness. Each simulated dataset will be fitted with the same model intended for the final analysis, and convergence, bias, interval coverage, and power or precision will be summarized across candidate enrollment sizes. The chosen smallest meaningful time ratio and its supporting assumptions will be documented before recruitment. Synthetic pilot values used to test the workflow will be labeled as such and will not be presented as empirical variance estimates.
edits.reason: Presents the simulation workflow as a connected procedure rather than a list of separate sentences.

edits.old: Tracking loss can affect guidance and measurement simultaneously. A trial with sparse gaze coverage may have valid selection timing but unreliable gaze-contact latency. Exclusion should therefore be measure-specific where justified. A missing gaze contact does not automatically invalidate completion time, and a complete motion stream does not repair missing voice playback events. Each analysis will report its denominator and reasons for missingness.
edits.new: Tracking loss can affect guidance and measurement simultaneously, though not always in the same way. A trial with sparse gaze coverage may have valid selection timing yet unreliable gaze-contact latency, so exclusion should be measure-specific where justified. A missing gaze contact does not automatically invalidate completion time, and a complete motion stream does not repair missing voice playback events. Each analysis will therefore report its own denominator and reasons for missingness.
edits.reason: Tightens the causal link from the example to the measure-specific exclusion rule.

edits.old: Baseline and final Simulator Sickness Questionnaire responses will describe symptom burden and pre-to-post change across the full exposure. Canonical scores will be calculated only from the intended item anchors and scoring rules. These measurements do not provide separate voice-block sickness effects because there is no between-block administration. Safety stops, discomfort reports, and incomplete exposure will be reported alongside symptom change; a numerical exclusion or stopping cutoff is not invented for this draft. The operational stopping procedure must be frozen before participant collection.

edits.reason: Brings the design reason forward and links the missing cutoff to the freeze requirement.

edits.old: The similarity manipulation check will report the paired difference between self-similar and catalog-voice ratings with uncertainty. A group-level decision rule and any practically meaningful difference remain open preregistration decisions. The study will not classify an individual as invalid merely because the clone is not recognized. Equivalence testing is not currently specified; a nonsignificant voice contrast will therefore not be interpreted as equivalence.
edits.new: The similarity manipulation check will report the paired difference between self-similar and catalog-voice ratings with uncertainty, whereas a group-level decision rule and any practically meaningful difference remain open preregistration decisions. The study will not classify an individual as invalid merely because the clone is not recognized. Because equivalence testing is not currently specified, a nonsignificant voice contrast will not be interpreted as equivalence.
edits.reason: Separates what is specified from what remains open, with clearer causal phrasing.

edits.old: This chapter distinguishes existing engineering records from participant results that have not yet been collected. The October 20 alignment audit documents software checks, analysis tests, and an Android build/install/launch. These records support specific implementation claims. They do not establish a treatment effect, a naturalness rating, eye-tracker accuracy, or acoustic response latency.

edits.old: A phrase can be geometrically admissible in isolation and still be poor guidance in sequence. Repeating a direction immediately after it was delivered can be unnecessary. A correct downward cue can become obsolete after the controller reaches the target. A gaze acknowledgment can arrive late after multiple model waits even though each individual response was well formed. Evaluation must therefore inspect recent state, actions, and actual speech around the event.
edits.new: A phrase can be geometrically admissible in isolation and still be poor guidance in sequence. Repeating a direction immediately after it was delivered can be unnecessary, and a correct downward cue can become obsolete once the controller reaches the target. Likewise, a gaze acknowledgment can arrive late after multiple model waits even though each individual response was well formed. Evaluation must therefore inspect recent state, actions, and actual speech around the event.
edits.reason: Turns a list of examples into connected support for the thesis sentence.

edits.old: The deterministic checks will establish whether the evidence supports an action. They will distinguish gaze confirmation, controller confirmation, and trial completion. A model judge may then assess wording, timing, repetition, and interruption appropriateness using that evidence. Its ratings remain advisory. They are not human-perceived correctness and do not convert an incompletely logged episode into a known success or failure.
edits.new: Deterministic checks will first establish whether the evidence supports an action, distinguishing gaze confirmation, controller confirmation, and trial completion. A model judge may then use that evidence to assess the appropriateness of wording, timing, repetition, and interruption. Its ratings remain advisory: they do not represent human-perceived correctness, and they cannot convert an incompletely logged episode into a known success or failure.
edits.reason: Combines stunted sentences and keeps the order of deterministic checks before advisory judging.

edits.old: \textbf{Protocol proposal.} The engineering evaluation will maintain three explicitly labeled sources of cases. Scripted fixtures will exercise known transitions and fault conditions. A development corpus will contain recorded sequences used to identify faults and tune policy. A separate evaluation corpus will be held out from those tuning decisions. At this stage, no frozen split, sample count, or completed held-out score is claimed.
edits.new: \textbf{Protocol proposal.} The engineering evaluation will maintain three explicitly labeled sources of cases: scripted fixtures that exercise known transitions and fault conditions, a development corpus of recorded sequences used to identify faults and tune policy, and a separate evaluation corpus held out from those tuning decisions. At this stage, no frozen split, sample count, or completed held-out score is claimed.
edits.reason: Gives the three-part enumeration an integrated structure.

edits.old: Wrong-direction and stale hints will be labeled only when the available evidence shows the instruction is unhelpful toward the task. A different but valid phrase is not automatically wrong. Missing evidence remains unknown. Repetition, unnecessary speech, excessive silence, and interruption appropriateness require context beyond a sign check on an angle.
edits.new: Wrong-direction and stale hints will be labeled only when the available evidence shows that the instruction is unhelpful toward the task; a different but valid phrase is not automatically wrong, and missing evidence remains unknown. Judgments about repetition, unnecessary speech, excessive silence, and interruption appropriateness likewise require context beyond a sign check on an angle.
edits.reason: Consolidates choppy labeling rules into a coherent criterion.

edits.old: An ordering failure can occur when a correction is queued before the controller reaches the target. If playback checks use the older snapshot, the correction can play immediately before a pointing acknowledgment. Another possibility is that the controller hold has not qualified yet and the ordinary-direction policy remains active during the hold. A third is that action priority admits a lower-priority cue despite newer pointing evidence. These causes require different fixes and cannot be distinguished from the spoken text alone.
edits.new: An ordering failure can occur when a correction is queued before the controller reaches the target, and several distinct mechanisms could produce it. If playback checks use the older snapshot, the correction can play immediately before a pointing acknowledgment. Alternatively, the controller hold may not yet have qualified, leaving the ordinary-direction policy active during the hold, or action priority may admit a lower-priority cue despite newer pointing evidence. These causes require different fixes, yet they cannot be distinguished from the spoken text alone.
edits.reason: Frames the alternatives up front and replaces the 'Another possibility / A third' list with connected prose.

edits.old: A separate reference-frame problem arises when an object appears higher than a highlighted neighbor but the instruction says to look lower. The instruction may be calculated relative to the current eye ray, which could lie above both. The phrase can then be geometrically consistent yet confusing because the highlight suggests a different reference object. Diagnosis requires the recorded gaze ray, object positions, highlighted candidate, and playback time. It must not rely only on the review camera's screen-space layout.
edits.new: A separate reference-frame problem arises when an object appears higher than a highlighted neighbor but the instruction says to look lower. If the instruction is calculated relative to the current eye ray, which could lie above both objects, the phrase can be geometrically consistent yet confusing because the highlight suggests a different reference object. Diagnosis therefore requires the recorded gaze ray, object positions, highlighted candidate, and playback time; it must not rely only on the review camera's screen-space layout.
edits.reason: Links the hypothesized cause to its consequence and to the diagnostic requirement.

edits.old: The primary result will include the fitted time contrast, its uncertainty, the analyzed participant and trial counts, and model diagnostics. Secondary sections will report workload and IMI subscales at participant-by-block level. Exploratory sections will report agent perception, voice experience, guidance behavior, and debrief themes. Tables will identify missing observations rather than silently change denominators.

edits.old: The inspected builder uses the model alias \texttt{typesafe-ai/jev}. Its base payload has a state and a questions object. The \texttt{navigation\_phrase} question has type \texttt{choice}; eligible phrase texts are keys in a \texttt{criteria} object. Their values carry tone, word count, semantic metadata, and a locally assigned geometric-validity flag. The builder requires two to five candidates and unique candidate texts. That local flag states the result of filtering at request time; it is not an independent model verification or a guarantee that the candidate will remain appropriate.

The builder requires two to five candidates and unique candidate texts. The local flag records the result of filtering at request time; it is not an independent model verification or a guarantee that the candidate will remain appropriate.
edits.reason: Integrates the payload structure description; all identifiers and the 2–5 constraint are kept.

edits.old: The parser requires the expected choice type and an exact member of the submitted alternatives. In the inspected request wrapper, validation occurs before a response is logged as accepted. A syntactically valid but unsupported phrase is an invalid response. A valid response that says wait is a deferral, not a timeout. A valid speak response can still be canceled or rejected by the local scheduler after the state changes. Evaluation must preserve these distinctions.
edits.new: The parser requires the expected choice type and an exact member of the submitted alternatives, and in the inspected request wrapper this validation occurs before a response is logged as accepted. A syntactically valid but unsupported phrase is therefore an invalid response, whereas a valid response that says wait is a deferral rather than a timeout. Even a valid speak response can still be canceled or rejected by the local scheduler after the state changes. Evaluation must preserve these distinctions.
edits.reason: Connects the response categories with contrastive transitions; keeps the short concluding directive.

edits.old: The state is a snapshot of an observation, not a live connection to the participant. The relevant inspected request paths include \path{runtime.evidence.valid}, \path{runtime.evidence.guidanceState.newGuidanceAllowed}, \path{runtime.playback.is_speaking}, \path{runtime.playback.is_busy}, and \path{runtime.seconds_since_speech_ended}. The request also carries the locally built context and candidate semantics. These fields should be audited from the actual serialized payload whenever the adapter changes. This inspection did not establish whether voice-condition identifiers, voice IDs, or condition-linked tone requests appear in every enabled serialized request. Provider decisions cannot yet be assumed condition-blind. The frozen-payload audit must establish whether tone requests are held constant across voice conditions.

edits.old: Recent history is supplied under \path{runtime.playback.recent_history}. The memory object identifies its schema as \texttt{speech-memory-v1}, its reset scope, and its 15-second window. Speech entries record text, context, phase, allowed action, age, and whether playback started, completed, or was interrupted. State entries retain prior/current phase and transition reason. The queues contain at most four speech entries and four transitions. The current pending proposal is not treated as already spoken history.

edits.old: A reproduction report should distinguish three achievements. Rebuilding the software verifies that the source and dependencies can produce an application. Replaying recorded observations verifies a particular decision and timing interpretation under a stated simulator. A new wearer session tests the delivered interaction on actual hardware. None implies the others. In particular, fast simulated scheduling is not measured acoustic latency, and an offline alternative cannot show the participant's unobserved response to it.
edits.new: A reproduction report should distinguish three achievements, none of which implies the others. Rebuilding the software verifies that the source and dependencies can produce an application; replaying recorded observations verifies a particular decision and timing interpretation under a stated simulator; and a new wearer session tests the delivered interaction on actual hardware. In particular, fast simulated scheduling is not measured acoustic latency, and an offline alternative cannot show the participant's unobserved response to it.
edits.reason: States the independence of the three achievements up front and presents them as a single structured sentence.

cautions: Terminology: 07-evaluation.tex (Why Sequence Evaluation) and 06-analysis.tex say 'trial completion', while the design separates gaze confirmation, controller confirmation and trigger completion. I left the wording as it is. Consider saying 'right-trigger trial completion' so it matches the appendix's description of the round-manager path.
Citation: the Guo Q20--22 ratings in 06-analysis.tex have no citation key. The later verified-grounding pass should add one, and the item labels should be checked against the instrument.

Format review: two tables in 07-evaluation.tex ('Evidence status...' and 'Planned empirical results...') have no \label and no short caption, unlike the other tables. UCF format review may flag the inconsistent List of Tables entries.
Undefined term: 'Jev' appears in the evaluation chapter and table without being defined there. Check that it is introduced earlier (e.g., in Chapter ch:system) or add a short gloss.

Open design items stated in the text: no timeout threshold, stopping cutoff, smallest meaningful effect, multiplicity families or equivalence margin has been frozen. These need preregistration before collection, and the prose should not suggest otherwise.

Measurement gaps: the exact pre-cue theta snapshot and 20/20 vertical allocation are documented as implementation gaps. The candidate model cannot be fitted as written until they are fixed, so keep these caveats whenever the primary model is mentioned.

Inspection scope: the appendix's admission algorithm covers scheduler, playback and round-manager behavior that was outside the three-file inspection. Keep it labeled as a specification to verify, not as inspected behavior.

Analysis/design interaction: practice uses the first block's voice, which adds familiarity to that voice only. The carryover paragraph mentions this; consider also listing it as a sensitivity consideration in the order/period analysis.
No edits were made to main.tex because its abstract was not among the supplied files.
